data.title: Google Builds Simulated Internet to Test Chrome Browser Agents' Security
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Google’s Chrome security team has built an isolated testing environment called Mirror Dimension to assess browser agents’ ability to navigate websites, complete tasks and resist malicious instructions. It contains thousands of simulated websites across scenarios such as e-commerce and social media, supports multi-step tasks and can be reset to a clean state without affecting real websites.

The environment focuses on indirect prompt injection, in which malicious instructions embedded in webpage content or tool responses attempt to make agents take actions users did not request. Google can insert test payloads into text, images, accessibility labels and tool responses. The company says its automated red-team process enables each security engineer to generate and test more than 1,000 candidate cases per day.

data.title: Bill Ackman: Fed Should Replace 2% Inflation Target With 3%
data.description:
According to Jin10, Pershing Square CEO Bill Ackman said the Federal Reserve was about to make another mistake at its December 9 rate-setting meeting and should replace its 2% inflation target with a more realistic 3% target. He said financial conditions had tightened sharply: SpaceX recently obtained secured debt financing at an 8.259% interest rate, while the unsecured bonds it issued at its IPO carried a rate below 6%; the recent stock market decline had also significantly raised the cost of equity financing.

Ackman said pursuing a 2% inflation target was unreasonable given geopolitical risks, investment needs from global military spending, deglobalization and tariffs, and large-scale investment in AI infrastructure and related energy. He said these realities did not exist when the 2% target was set, and that if the Fed continued raising rates in an attempt to bring inflation down to 2%, it would push the U.S. and global economies into recession.

data.title: GPT-5.5 Bank Support Agent Scores Perfectly on Self-Test but Succeeds in Only 5 of 97 Held-Out Cases
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing CryptoSlate, Uniphore researchers found that a GPT-5.5 bank customer service agent earned a perfect score on tests written by its developers but succeeded in only five of 97 held-out cases reviewed by researchers. The agent assumed customers could not be found by name or email, despite those options being available in the simulation. Its own tests instead treated asking customers for an ID as the correct approach, and the agent then rejected other lookup methods.

AppSci-Bench covers seven simulated business workflows, including bank customer service, invoice review, customer relationship management and flight changes. Of 132 builds with recorded self-test results, 86 scored at least 99% on those tests. Across 13 Claude Opus 4.8 builds, iteration raised average self-test scores by 16.9 percentage points and held-out test scores by 3.2 points.

In a separate comparison of 252 builds, the difference in held-out scores between workflows with and without testing and iteration was not statistically significant.

data.title: Goldman Says U.S. Stock Fear Near Historic Extreme, Positioning Flushout Incomplete
data.description:
U.S. stocks have sold off sharply, with the Nasdaq 100 down 19.8% from its record high on October 6, near the bear-market threshold, and the S&P 500 down about 12%; the index fell 8.6% last week, its largest weekly decline in 19 months. The CBOE Volatility Index briefly approached 36, its highest level in 19 months.

According to Odaily, Goldman Sachs’ trading desk said market fear was nearing an extreme, with its volatility fear index reaching 9.8 out of 10 last Friday. Over the past month, systematic strategies such as commodity trading advisers sold about $57 billion in stocks, turning net U.S. equity positioning into a $19 billion short. Hedge funds have cut exposure substantially, but other investors remain heavily invested, and a broad positioning flushout sufficient to support a strong rebound has not occurred.

Goldman said most U.S. CTA selling may be complete and trend-following strategies could become buyers again if stocks rebound. However, risks from potential Federal Reserve rate hikes, uncertainty over returns on AI investment, and market liquidity pressures remain. Goldman said extreme fear does not mean the market has bottomed; tactical buying opportunities may exist, but a sustained rebound would require more positive catalysts.

data.title: Nscale Slows Hiring and Cuts Costs Ahead of Planned $35 Billion IPO
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, British data center operator Nscale is slowing hiring and cutting spending as it prepares for a $35 billion IPO, while streamlining and standardizing its operations. Two people familiar with the matter said Chief Operating Officer Justin Osofsky told employees in an internal email this month that hiring would be paused for the coming months, except for critical roles. The company will also cut nonessential spending. The hiring slowdown does not cover data center construction jobs and mainly affects back-office roles.

Nscale, a startup backed by Nvidia, has Cheryl Sandberg, a former Meta executive, and Nick Clegg, a former UK deputy prime minister, on its board. The company must decide whether to list this year as planned or postpone the IPO until 2027. Its workforce grew from about 300 in early 2026 to about 1,100. Recent declines across AI stocks, investor concerns about debt, and the sudden departure of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang have cast uncertainty over its listing plans. CoreWeave shares fell nearly 30% and Nebius shares nearly 50% over the past month.

This month, Nscale warned it would need additional financing to meet its expected commitments for next year. It estimated revenue of $307 million and a net loss of nearly $1.7 billion for the nine months through September. Two people familiar with its listing plans said Nscale had hoped that Anthropic’s high-profile IPO this week would ease concerns about the AI market and allow it to begin its roadshow within weeks. Anthropic shares, after initially rising above their offering price, fell back to that price during Friday’s broad technology-stock selloff. Nscale has not set a listing timetable, the two people said.

data.title: Billionaire Bill Ackman Warns Further Fed Rate Hikes Could Trigger U.S. Recession
data.description:
Billionaire hedge fund manager Bill Ackman warned that further Federal Reserve rate increases could push the U.S. economy into recession. According to Odaily, Ackman wrote on X that the Fed could make another mistake on December 9, as financial conditions have already tightened significantly.

He cited SpaceX, which recently obtained secured debt financing at an 8.259% interest rate, compared with a rate below 6% on unsecured bonds issued at its IPO. Ackman also said the recent sharp decline in stocks had significantly raised the cost of equity financing.

Ackman said a 2% inflation target does not fit the current economic environment. Geopolitical risks, rising global military spending, deglobalization, tariffs, and large-scale investment in AI infrastructure and energy could sustain inflationary pressure, he said. He argued that a 3% inflation target would be more realistic and warned that continued rate increases to bring inflation back to 2% could cause a recession in the U.S. and globally.

data.title: CICC: Copper’s Bottom May Be Anchored at $12,500 per Ton
data.description: According to Jin10, a CICC report said copper supply growth from mines is relatively limited and could be revised lower amid various disruptions. AI is expected to provide a considerable boost to demand, while structural inventory tightness caused by U.S. tariffs is likely to persist. Tight supply and demand could drive prices higher. However, slower revenue growth at large-model companies and worsening financing conditions could delay data center construction. If demand temporarily falls short of expectations, copper price volatility could increase; tighter macro liquidity could also weigh on prices, leaving them at risk of a correction in a relatively conservative scenario. Copper prices could be highly volatile over the year, with the bottom potentially anchored at an incentive price of $12,500 per ton and the upper limit at $14,500 per ton. The midpoint is expected to rise further compared with 2026.

data.title: PRECIOUS METALS | China's Gold Buying Holds $1 Trillion Trade Surplus in Check
data.description: According to Bloomberg, China's gold imports surged to a record $209 billion so far this year in an unprecedented buying spree that followed top officials' promise to make the country the world's marketplace rather than just its factory. The gold buying is keeping China's $1 trillion trade surplus in check.
